content.title: About
content.content: Gin and tonic is a classic cocktail made of gin, tonic water, ice, and often a slice of lime. Gin is a distilled spirit flavored with juniper berries and various botanicals. Tonic water is a carbonated beverage that contains quinine, giving it a distinctive bitter taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first recorded combination of gin and tonic dates back to the 19th century, when British officers in India used quinine tonic to prevent malaria.
Traditionally served in a highball glass with plenty of ice and a lime wedge.
There are many gin styles: London dry, botanical-infused (cucumber, rosemary, etc.), and regional varieties, each imparting a unique character.
Tonic can be classic or flavored (berry, citrus, spice) to alter the drink’s profile.
In some countries, a "salted rim" gin‑tonic is popular, where sea salt is sprinkled on the glass edge to enhance flavor.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Quinine in tonic has antioxidant properties, and juniper berries in gin provide flavonoids.

items.title: Moderate consumption may promote relaxation
items.content: Alcohol in moderate amounts can have a calming effect and help reduce stress.

items.title: Vitamin C from lime
items.content: The lime garnish adds vitamin C, supporting the immune system.

items.title: Alcohol
items.content: Excessive alcohol intake can lead to liver issues, dependence, and other health problems.

items.title: Quinine
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to quinine, including rash and headaches.

items.title: Sugar content in tonic
items.content: Many tonic waters contain added sugar, increasing the drink’s calories and affecting blood glucose levels.

content.title: How to Make
content.content: Pour 50 ml of gin into a glass, fill with ice, add 150–200 ml of tonic water, stir gently, and garnish with a lime or lemon wedge. Optional additions include a sprig of rosemary or a few juniper berries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the gin bottle in a cool, dark place with the cap tightly sealed. Once opened, keep tonic water refrigerated to preserve freshness and flavor.
